newsitem.title: ITALY: European mission leaves Rome for Albania.
newsitem.headline: European mission leaves Rome for Albania.

text.p: An advance team of European experts left Rome for Tirana on Wednesday to assess the scale of a planned multinational relief operation in troubled Albania.
An Italian government plane left Rome's Ciampino military airport for the Albanian capital at around 1500 GMT with members of the team on board.
The team, of about 15 people, included experts from the 54-nation Organisation for Security and Cooperation in Europe (OSCE), the European Union and its Commission and the Council of Europe.
The delegation, the second of its kind in two weeks, is due to meet Prime Minister Bashkim Fino and other ministers.
"This is the start of a more permanent mission which in its turn will last for a couple of months," Jan de Marchant et d'Ansembourg, the senior Dutch diplomat leading the team, said.
He said the larger mission would aim to provide emergency relief, security for mission members and aid distribution, and help for Albania to prepare for early general elections by June.
"We do foresee problems but are not counting on them," d'Ansembourg said.
Albania has been swept by violence since January when a series of popular but fraudulent investment schemes collapsed wiping out millions of dollars in savings.
Riots and protests against the schemes were followed by a popular uprising in the south with thousands of people seizing weapons from army depots and setting up rebel councils.
Military experts from European countries scouted Albania on Wednesday to prepare for a possible multinational protection force to accompany the mission.
In Vienna, OSCE ambassadors were close to agreeing on a framework for a broad international military force, made up of volunteer nations, diplomatic sources said.
